newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - European bourses make big gains on U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - European bourses make big gains on U.S. data.

text.p: European bourses made healthy gains on Thursday as a drop in the U.S. trade deficit lifted Wall Street, delivering its third rally in as many days.
On currency markets, the better-than-expected U.S. trade figures also pulled the dollar up half a pfennig against the mark. But late profit-taking wiped out most of the advance.

Europe's optimistic mood was underpinned by the buoyancy in New York. Bourses on both sides of the Atlantic rose in pre-Christmas holiday business on Wednesday and the pattern was much the same on Thursday.

The Dow Jones industrials powered ahead 0.75 percent after figures showed the U.S. trade gap narrowed sharply in October as overseas sales of aircraft surged. New York had climbed 38 points to 6,346 on Wednesday in an end-of-year rush to snap up technology stocks.

London climbed 0.8 percent at the close. Trading was also enlivened by a pre-Christmas bidding spree with companies going shopping for takeover targets, putting a price tag of more than two billion pounds ($3.3 billion) on their list of potential purchases.
Firms have launched five major bids for British companies this week -- most of them hostile -- injecting life into the normally dull holiday period for dealmakers.
Dealers believe London's FTSE index could test its all-time highs in the next few days, provided Wall Street maintains its current upward momentum.
"This is all about the Dow. It's had a pretty rough time the past few weeks but seems to be bouncing back," one senior dealer said. "We're(UK share market)are just along for the ride."

Trading volume was over 950 million shares, the highest level since April. "The better volume is encouraging. At the beginning of the weak it looked as though the market was winding down for Christmas," another dealer said.

Paris was the best performer, showing a gain of 1.34 percent at the close. Market spirits were lifted by New York and a flurry of merger-related announcements in the pharmaceuticals and retail sectors.
Elf Aquitaine and Sanofi rose strongly after Elf said it would be desirable for its pharmaceutical unit Sanofi to merge with other laboratories to boost profitability.

In Frankfurt, stocks on the computerised IBIS index jumped on the U.S. trade figures and were up 0.4 percent in late trade. Floor trading, which ended before the U.S. data was issued, finished down 0.46 percent.
On the currency front, the dollar climbed half a pfennig on the U.S. trade figures before profit-takers eroded much of the gain towards the end of the session.
But U.S. currency remained strong against the yen after Tokyo shares tumbled overnight to their low of the year amid deepening gloom about Japan's economic outlook.

But the details of the trade report showed the politically sensitive trade gap with Japan surging again. The gap rose 30.9 percent to $4.96 billion, the highest since August 1995 because of increased car and car parts imports.
Some U.S. manufacturers contend Japan is deliberately manipulating its currency to keep the yen's value low and make its products cheaper for American importers.
The Swiss franc was lower in Europe and set a two-year low at 1.3372 per dollar and a three-year low at 85.82 centimes per mark at one point.
CURRENCIES
The dollar was quoted around 1.5560 marks and 113.95 yen, compared with 1.5541 and 113.65 in late business on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares ended 33.1 points higher at 4,051.3.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index finished up 29.81 at 2,248.70.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed down 13.00 at 2,807.75. The after-hours IBIS index was up 10.60 points at 2824.83.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold finished unchanged at $369.10 an ounce. Silver was at $4.87, up one cent.
